13:15 Yeah! Though I have not started speaking in English due to various reasons, I have learnt a lot through ChatGPT. And I always spend disproportionate time on it, mostly focusing on my English grammar, vocabulary, collocations, various registers of writing, sentence usages of words I newly encounter across news, social media, or so. And I feel substantially and sufficiently confident in my understanding in that part of my English journey.

However, the most incredible method of learning English that I have developed myself throughout this journey is that I would check my comments consistently for grammar in ChatGPT. I consume a lot of content on YouTube, and sometimes X, and I love to pour my thoughts out on the content I consume — mostly in English. Earlier, I would myself edit the comment, then by ChatGPT, and only thereafter I would make it live on the comment box. But now I have made a change: I now mostly check for grammatical correctness only after droping the comment. It is because now I feel that I make mistakes but not so much that I need to edit it before commenting on such platforms where our identity is almost completely obscure. However, I still check my comment for grammatical mistakes, register sophistication, and tone to learn more and improve my command over English.

This long comment is also a step in that direction. 😂😂
